original_interpretation: Entegris has recently added manufacturing in Kaohsiung Science Park (Taiwan) and Colorado Springs (US) to be closer to new fabs.
evidence_found: "Recent examples of this strategy include our new facilities in Kaohsiung Science Park (“KSP”) in Taiwan and in Colorado Springs as well as our new Korea Technology Center"; "We further enhanced this footprint with our KSP facility in Taiwan, our new Colorado Springs manufacturing facility" (10-K FY2025, Item 1)
notes: Strategy sentence: 'to better serve our global customers as they build new fabs in various countries and seek reliable local supply chain partners', so 'closer to new fabs' is fair. Opened via web_extract (full text file). Colorado Springs has up to $77.0m CHIPS Act award per same passage.

original_interpretation: Merck KGaA's Semiconductor Solutions unit consists of Thin Films, Formulations (patterning incl. photoresists, and CMP planarization), Specialty Gases, and Delivery Systems & Services.
evidence_found: "Our Semiconductor Solutions business unit consists of the Thin Films, Formulations, Specialty Gases, and Delivery Systems & Services business fields." "The portfolio of the Formulations business field is divided into the areas of Patterning and Planarization. It includes lithography products such as photoresists ... The Planarization business encompasses materials for chemical-mechanical planarization" (AR 2025, Electronics)

original_interpretation: Asia-Pacific generated 72% of Merck KGaA's Electronics net sales in 2025; Electronics was 17% of group sales.
evidence_found: "Electronics accounted for 17% of Group sales in 2025 ... In 2025, Asia-Pacific generated 72% of Electronics’ net sales, with Europe and North America accounting for 26% of sales." (AR 2025, Electronics)
notes: Remaining ~2% is other regions (not stated). Electronics is now Semiconductor Solutions + Optronics after the Surface Solutions sale on 31 July 2025, so 2025 includes seven months of Surface Solutions unless restated; the page does not say.

original_interpretation: Merck KGaA inaugurated its largest Semiconductor Solutions megasite in Kaohsiung, Taiwan in December 2025.
evidence_found: "In December 2025, we inaugurated our largest Semiconductor Solutions megasite in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, strengthening our global semiconductor supply chain resilience" (AR 2025, Electronics)

original_interpretation: Merck's MEGASYS Total Gas and Chemical Services staff operate and maintain gas and chemical delivery systems at many fab sites, an outsourced on-site service model.
evidence_found: "At many of the industry’s sites, production facilities and delivery systems are operated and maintained by our MEGASYS® Total Gas and Chemical Services employees." (AR 2025, Electronics, Delivery Systems & Services)
notes: 'Outsourced on-site service model' is a fair description of fab sites run by Merck staff; it is the researcher's wording, not Merck's. Correctly typed reported_claim.

original_interpretation: Shin-Etsu's semiconductor materials range includes silicon wafers, photoresists, photomask blanks, synthetic quartz and semiconductor encapsulating materials.
evidence_found: "Semiconductor silicon, Rare earth magnets, Semiconductor encapsulating materials, LED packaging materials, Photoresists, Photomask blanks, Synthetic quartz products" (Electronics Materials, Major Products); also "silicon wafers, photoresists, photomask blanks, and encapsulants"
notes: List is the Electronics Materials segment's major products; the claim keeps only the semiconductor items, which is correct. Shin-Etsu also lists pellicles.

original_interpretation: Shin-Etsu made Mimasu Semiconductor Industry, its long-time outsourced wafer-polishing partner, a wholly owned subsidiary in November 2024 after an August 2024 tender offer.
evidence_found: "We completed the tender offer for Mimasu Semiconductor Industry Co., Ltd. in August 2024, and after the subsequent formalities, it became a wholly owned subsidiary in November. ... We traditionally outsourced tasks such as polishing silicon wafers to Mimasu Semiconductor Industry, and as long-term partners" (AR 2025, Electronics Materials topic)
notes: Same passage: Shin-Etsu took 27.1% in 2005 and 40.5% in 2006.

original_interpretation: Shin-Etsu said its 300 mm wafer sales in Q1 FY2025 (April-June 2025) were made on a long-term agreement (LTA) basis.
evidence_found: "In the case of 300 mm wafers, Q1 sales were made on a long-term agreement (LTA) basis, so the results cited above are due to the reversal of inventory adjustments made in the previous quarter." (Q1 call summary, 24 Jul 2025, Electronics Materials Q&A)
notes: Context: 300 mm shipments rose by double digits YoY and QoQ; Shin-Etsu puts this down to LTA volumes after customers adjusted inventory the previous quarter. Q1 = April-June 2025 (FY ending March 2026).

original_interpretation: Shin-Etsu estimates that just under 20% of 300 mm DRAM wafers are used for HBM and just under 10% of 300 mm logic wafers for AI logic.
evidence_found: "For 300 mm DRAM wafers, we estimate that those used for AI memory (HBM) account for just under 20%, while for 300 mm logic wafers, those used for AI logic account for just under 10%." (Q1 call summary, 24 Jul 2025, Q&A)
notes: Company estimate, correctly typed. Population is wafers (not stated as starts vs shipments).

original_interpretation: Tokyo Ohka Kogyo reports a 26.1% global share of semiconductor photoresists (projected 2025 shipment volume, per Fuji Chimera Research), the top position.
evidence_found: Rendered page: "TOK has the top share of the global market for semiconductor photoresists." "Global market share for semiconductor photoresists 26.1%" "(based on projected shipment volume in 2025*)" "*Source: Fuji Chimera Research Institute, Current Status and Future Outlook of Innovative/Noticeable Semiconductor-Related Markets 2026"
notes: The numbers are HTML text, not an image. web_extract dropped them, so I checked them in the browser-rendered page. Volume share from a projected (not actual) 2025 figure by a third-party firm, cited by TOK. reported_claim is right.

original_interpretation: TOK reports photoresist shares by type of 29.3% EUV, 14.4% ArF, 33.3% KrF and 25.3% g/i-line (projected 2025 volume, Fuji Chimera).
evidence_found: Rendered page: "EUV photoresists 29.3%" "ArF excimer laser photoresists 14.4%" "KrF excimer laser photoresists 33.3%" "g/i-Line photoresists 25.3%" under "TOK’s market share for semiconductor photoresists (based on projected shipment volume in 2025*)"
notes: Checked in the browser-rendered page. Source: Fuji Chimera Research Institute (2026 edition).

original_interpretation: Resonac's Semiconductor and Electronic Materials segment covers front-end materials (high-purity electronic gases, CMP slurry) and back-end materials (epoxy molding compounds, die bonding materials, copper clad laminates, photosensitive films and solder resists).
evidence_found: "Main Products - Front-end Semiconductor Materials: High-purity gases for electronics, CMP slurry - Back-end Semiconductor Materials: Epoxy molding compounds, Die bonding materials, Copper clad laminates, Photosensitive dry films, Photosensitive solder resists - Device Solutions: HD media, SiC epitaxial wafers" (FY2025 results deck, p. 10)
notes: The segment also includes Device Solutions (HD media, SiC epi wafers), which the claim leaves out. 2025 segment revenue: ¥506.3bn (front-end ¥83.6bn, back-end ¥245.0bn).

original_interpretation: JSR, a major photoresist maker, came under JICC-02 (owned by JIC funds) control via a tender offer completed 16 April 2024 and was set to delist from the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
evidence_found: "a tender offer ... which had been conducted by JICC-02, Ltd. ... since March 19, 2024 ... has been completed as of April 16, 2024." "the Tender Offeror will become a new parent company" "JIC PEFJ1 Limited Partnership: 97%" "the Company Shares are scheduled to be delisted" (JSR notice, 17 Apr 2024)
notes: Correct as of the notice: JICC-02 held 84.36% of voting rights after settlement on 23 Apr 2024. Newer: JSR was delisted on 25 June 2024 (JSR notice of 24 June 2024), recorded as a new claim. 'Major photoresist maker' is not in this source.

original_interpretation: Siltronic says price pressure outside long-term agreements hit its 2025 results; 2025 sales were EUR 1,347 million.
evidence_found: "In addition to negative currency effects, price pressure outside of long-term contracts had a particularly negative impact." "With sales of EUR 1,347 million, we are – as projected – below the level of the previous year." (AR 2025, Interview with the Executive Board); key figures: Sales 2025 1,346.7 (EUR m)
notes: Key-figures table: EUR 1,346.7m (2024: 1,412.8m). Management attribution, so this is closer to reported_claim than fact for the price-pressure part; the sales figure is audited.

original_interpretation: Siltronic's new 300 mm fab in Singapore completed many customer qualifications in 2025, and it closed its SD line in Burghausen, Germany.
evidence_found: "This includes key customer qualifications at the new 300 mm fab in Singapore and the closure of our SD line in Burghausen." "we were able to complete many important customer qualifications over the past twelve months" (AR 2025, Executive Board interview)
notes: SD line closure cut sales by a single-digit percent and has its first full-year effect in 2026. The Singapore ramp is slowing because demand is below plan.

original_interpretation: Linde's on-site (pipeline) supply contracts are typically total-requirement contracts of 10-20 years with minimum purchase requirements and price escalation.
evidence_found: "On-site product supply contracts generally are total requirement contracts with terms typically ranging from 10-20 years and containing minimum purchase requirements and price escalation provisions." (Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1, Distribution)
notes: This covers all Linde on-site customers, not only electronics/fabs.

original_interpretation: Linde's merchant (bulk liquid) customer agreements are usually three- to seven-year requirement contracts.
evidence_found: "The customer agreements used in the merchant business are usually three to seven-year requirement contracts." (Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1, Merchant)
notes: This covers all Linde merchant customers, not only electronics.

original_interpretation: Air Liquide's Electronics revenue grew 3.1% in 2025 (6.1% excluding equipment and installation), with carrier gases up more than 10% after seven new production units started.
evidence_found: Asia Pacific section (p. 13-14): "Electronics revenue was up +3.1% in 2025, and +6.1% excluding Equipment & Installation sales. Carrier gases sales posted strong growth of more than +10% ... seven new production units". Group (p. 3-4): "In Electronics (+1.2%), the normalization of Equipment & Installation sales ... masked dynamic growth in the rest of the business (+5.8%)"; table "Electronics 2,510 2,465 -1.8% +1.2%"
correction: The +3.1% / +6.1% / carrier gases >10% figures are for Air Liquide's Asia Pacific region only. Group Electronics revenue was EUR 2,465m in 2025: +1.2% comparable, -1.8% published, +5.8% excluding Equipment & Installation. See new claims (one supersedes this claim).
notes: The quoted sentence is in the Asia Pacific regional section. Americas Electronics was -2.5% (+8.5% excl. E&I).

original_interpretation: TECHCET expected 6% growth in the global chip manufacturing materials market in 2025, with total revenue exceeding US$87bn by 2029.
evidence_found: Archived original (Wayback capture 2025-12-31): "is anticipating growth of 6% for the global semiconductor chip manufacturing materials market in 2025. AI-related device demand continues to push wafer starts upwards with total revenue exceeding $87 B USD by 2029." Same release later: "pushing overall materials revenues up in the 8% to 10% range for the year."
correction: Release contradicts itself: the 6% headline and a later '8% to 10% range for the year' (carried over from TECHCET's January 2025 release, which forecast ~8%). Market definition not disclosed; not comparable with SEMI's US$73.2bn.
notes: Live SRC-0617 URL now redirects to techinsights.com (TECHCET is now part of TechInsights), so I checked an archived copy. The figures match. TECHCET's newer release (15 Jan 2026) gives no new total.

original_interpretation: TECHCET estimated 2024 CMP consumables revenue at about US$3.4bn: slurries about US$2bn and pads US$1.39bn.
evidence_found: "In 2024, the CMP consumables market showed modest growth of 1.6%, reaching an estimated US $3.4 billion. Slurry revenues increased just over 1% to US $2 billion, while pad revenues rose by 2% to US $1.39 billion." (Semiconductor Digest, TECHCET release)
notes: SRC-0618 is Semiconductor Digest (industry press) running TECHCET's 11 June 2025 release word for word. The techcet.com original appeared only in search results and the live site redirects. source_type research_firm reflects the content's origin, not the publisher.

original_interpretation: TECHCET forecast CMP consumables revenue of about US$3.6bn in 2025 and an 8.6% CAGR through 2029.
evidence_found: "TECHCET forecasts nearly a 6% increase in CMP consumables revenue in 2025, reaching approximately US $3.6 billion ... the CMP consumables market is projected to grow at an 8.6% CAGR through 2029." (Semiconductor Digest, TECHCET release)
notes: A forecast made in June 2025, correctly typed estimate. CAGR base year not stated (likely 2024-2029).

original_interpretation: TECHCET flags sourcing of rare-earth abrasives for CMP slurries as a key supply-chain challenge, with suppliers working to diversify beyond China.
evidence_found: "Geopolitical and trade issues, particularly regarding the sourcing of rare earth abrasives, will remain a key supply chain challenge, as suppliers work to diversify beyond China." (Semiconductor Digest, TECHCET release)
notes: This is a qualitative analyst view, not a numeric estimate. The type is acceptable.

original_interpretation: TECHCET forecast the 2025 electronic gases market at US$6.34bn (+4.8%), with specialty gases up 5.2% and bulk gases up 3.8%.
evidence_found: "the global electronic gas market will grow by 4.8% year-over-year in 2025 to reach $6.34 billion. This includes 5.2% growth in Specialty Gases and 3.8% growth in Bulk Gases" (Semiconductor Digest, TECHCET 2025-26 Electronic Gases CMR summary)
notes: Forecast. Same release: 2024-2029 CAGR 5.0% (specialty 5.3%, bulk 4.1%).

original_interpretation: TECHCET's electronic gases report names Air Liquide, Linde, Nippon Sanso, Air Products and Resonac among the assessed suppliers.
evidence_found: "supplier assessments (Air Liquide, Linde, Nippon Sanso, Air Products, Resonac and more)" (Semiconductor Digest, TECHCET release)

original_interpretation: TECHCET says tariffs and US-China tensions are driving localisation and reshoring of gas supply, with Chinese and Korean start-ups seeking global scale.
evidence_found: "Tariff policies, and US-China tensions are driving localization and reshoring of materials supply." "Suppliers are responding with regional expansions, while startups in China and Korea seek global scale." (Semiconductor Digest, TECHCET release)
notes: The release says 'materials supply' in general, in the gases context. It also notes Asian fabs in the US still source specialty gases from Asia.

original_interpretation: TECHCET put 2025 wet chemicals and specialty cleans revenue at about US$5.44bn (+6%), on shipments of 2,706 million kg (+5%).
evidence_found: "shipments growth at +5% for 2025 to total 2,706 M Kg, with revenues up +6% to US $5,440M." (Semiconductor Digest, TECHCET Wet Chemicals update)
notes: A 2025 estimate/forecast made during 2025 (the release promotes the 28-29 Oct 2025 CMC seminar). 2024-2029 CAGR +6% for both shipments and revenue.

evidence_found: "Global supply remains balanced with demand, though most UHP production is concentrated in Asia. Localized capacity in the US and Europe is slowly emerging, but many planned expansions are on hold due to fab delays and trade tensions." (Semiconductor Digest, TECHCET Wet Chemicals update)

original_interpretation: TECHCET projects photolithography materials revenue to grow at a 5.4% CAGR from 2025 to 2030 to more than US$6.65bn, with resists growing slowest (4.2%).
evidence_found: Rendered article (Shannon Davis, 18 Feb 2026): "Total photolithography materials revenue is projected to grow at a 5.4% CAGR from 2025 to 2030 reaching more than $6,650 USD M, with ancillaries growing at 6.5% ... extensions growing at 5.8% ... and resists 4.2%" (2025-2026 Critical Materials Report on Photolithography, linked TECHCET)
notes: web_extract returned only the header, so I read the article in the browser. Publication date is 18 Feb 2026, set via updates.jsonl. TECHCET's own release (17 Feb 2026, techcet.com) appeared only in search results with the same wording.

original_interpretation: Ajinomoto says its Build-up Film (ABF) insulates the circuit substrates of high-performance CPUs in most of the world's personal computers.
evidence_found: Page HTML (section 'The standard for high-performance CPUs'): "Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) can be found at the heart of most of the world’s personal computers, where it provides electrical insulation of complex circuit substrates for high-performance central processing units (CPUs)."
notes: The text is in the page HTML but not in the visible innerText (JS layout), so I checked it in the DOM. This is marketing (reported_claim) and gives no share figure.

original_interpretation: SUMCO management said commodity 200 mm wafer prices declined in Q4 2025 (specialty products aside), while legacy-node wafer demand stayed weak.
evidence_found: "On prices, LTA prices are, by and large, being respected. ... We don't have many 200-millimeter LTAs. So reflecting supply/demand, 200-millimeter prices were generally softer. Setting aside specialty products, commodity 200-millimeter wafer prices declined. The outlook for Q1 is for continued solid volumes in 300-millimeter ... Demand for legacy node wafers remains lackluster." (earningsapi transcript, 10 Feb 2026)
correction: Quote matches, but the period is not clear. The passage follows 'The Q4 results were as discussed' and talks about 'last year'. It does not say whether commodity 200 mm prices fell in Q4 2025 or over 2025.
notes: Third-party transcript (tier 3). A Yahoo/Quartr transcript in search results has the same wording. SUMCO's own deck could not be opened (sumcosi.com IR pages returned nothing). The LTA-price passage is now a new claim.

original_interpretation: SUMCO said its LTAs set total volumes only, not a split between legacy and leading-edge wafers, so customers had to keep taking legacy wafers.
evidence_found: "However, when we entered into contracts with customers, there was no specification of volumes for legacy or leading edge because no one knew and the contracts were simply for total volume. ... our customers have no choice but to buy legacy wafers because that is what the contracts stipulate" (Hashimoto, Q&A #9, 10 Feb 2026)
notes: Third-party transcript (tier 3), so confidence stays low. The wording matches.

original_interpretation: SUMCO said 300 mm wafer demand fell 11% in 2023, then rose 2% in 2024 and 9% in 2025, while 200 mm fell 21%, 13% and 4%.
evidence_found: "200-millimeter fell 21% in 2023, 13% in 2024 and a further 4% in 2025." "300-millimeter was down 11% in 2023, but was up 2% in 2024 and up 9% in 2025." (10 Feb 2026 call, slides on 200 mm / 300 mm wafer trends)
correction: Numbers match. The transcript only says 'trend for 300-millimeter wafers' and never says what is measured (industry demand, shipments in area, or SUMCO's own sales). Calling it 'demand' is the researcher's reading. Treat as SUMCO's view of the market trend.
notes: Third-party transcript (tier 3). A Yahoo/Quartr transcript in search results has the same numbers.

original_interpretation: SEMI's regional materials figures measure where materials are consumed (ship-to region), not where they are produced, so they do not show production geography.
evidence_found: Checked inputs: MMDS sheet: "Historical annual revenue of semiconductor materials by category and “ship-to” market region"; "Data is compiled from actual inputs by material suppliers". SEMI 2024 release: "Taiwan, with $20.1 billion in revenue, was the world's largest consumer of semiconductor materials"
notes: The reasoning follows: suppliers report revenue by ship-to region, and SEMI calls regions 'consumers'. So the regions show where materials are delivered, not where they are made.

original_interpretation: Company segments do not map onto SEMI categories: Entegris combines CMP, deposition precursors, implant gases and filtration; Merck combines resists, CMP and specialty gases; Resonac spans fab gases and packaging mold compounds. SEMI segment totals therefore cannot be rebuilt from company segment revenue.
evidence_found: Checked inputs: SEMI taxonomy (Fab: Silicon, SOI, Photomasks, Photoresist, Ancillaries, Gases, Chemicals, Targets, CMP; Packaging: ... Mold Compounds ...); Entegris 10-K: MS = CVD/ALD deposition, CMP slurries and pads, implant gases, etch/clean; APS = filtration, purification; Merck: Thin Films, Formulations (photoresists, CMP), Specialty Gases, DS&S; Resonac: high-purity gases, CMP slurry, epoxy molding compounds
notes: The reasoning follows. Each company's segments cut across several SEMI categories and include things SEMI does not count as materials (Entegris filtration, Merck delivery systems, Resonac Device Solutions). Entegris splits these across two segments; 'combines' means company-wide.
